Direct, indirect and total effects of a ZISAR model

Source: R/effects.R
zisar_effects.Rd

Decomposes the effect of each covariate on the expected count \(E[y] = (1 - \pi)\mu\) into a direct part (a unit's own covariate), an indirect part (spillovers from the covariates of other units through the spatial multiplier) and their sum, averaged over units as in LeSage and Pace (2009).

Usage

zisar_effects(object, B = 500, level = 0.95)

# S3 method for class 'zisar_effects'
print(x, digits = 4, ...)

Arguments

object

A fitted "zisar" object.

B

Number of simulation draws for standard errors and intervals; 0 gives point estimates only.

level

Confidence level of the simulation intervals.

x

A "zisar_effects" object.

digits

Number of decimal places to print.

...

Not used.

Value

A data frame of class "zisar_effects", one row per covariate and effect (direct, indirect, total), with the point estimate and, when B > 0, the simulation standard error and interval bounds.

Details

The matrix of partial derivatives of \(E[y_i]\) with respect to \(x_{jr}\) is \(\mathrm{diag}(d)\, S(\rho)\, \beta_r\) with \(d_i = (1 - \pi_i)\mu_i\) and \(S(\rho) = (I - \rho W)^{-1}\). The average direct effect is the mean of its diagonal, the average total effect the mean of its row sums, and the indirect effect their difference. Only the diagonal and the row sums of \(S(\rho)\) are computed, so no dense \(n \times n\) matrix is formed for large \(n\).

A covariate that also enters the zero-inflation part (same name in both parts of the formula) adds the inflation channel \(-\mu_i \pi_i (1 - \pi_i) \gamma_r\), which acts on the unit itself only and so enters the direct and total effects. A covariate of the inflation part alone has this direct effect only. With the SAR filter on the inflation predictor (zero_spatial = "sar") the inflation channel passes through \(S_0 = (I - \rho_0 W)^{-1}\) as well, and has an indirect part.

Standard errors and intervals are simulation-based: parameters are drawn from their estimated asymptotic normal distribution and the effects recomputed for each draw, keeping the predicted random effects \(\hat u = (I - \rho W)\hat\eta - X\beta\) (and an inflation field at its mode) at their estimates. For \(n > 3000\), the diagonal of \(S(\rho)\) along the draws is interpolated between seven exact evaluations.

References

LeSage, J. and Pace, R. K. (2009). Introduction to Spatial Econometrics. Chapman and Hall/CRC.

Examples

set.seed(1)
sim <- rzisar(12, beta = c(1, 0.5), rho = 0.4, gamma = c(-1, 0.8))
fit <- zisar(y ~ x1 | z1, data = sim$data, W = sim$W)
zisar_effects(fit, B = 200)
#> ZISAR average effects on E[y] (simulation SEs, B = 200)
#> 
#>              Direct        Indirect            Total
#> x1  3.4788 (1.4814) 0.4043 (1.6099)  3.8832 (1.7326)
#> z1 -0.9652 (0.4093) 0.0000 (0.0000) -0.9652 (0.4093)
